title: Pluggable request context sentinels for resilient telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a small, pluggable runtime abstraction ("sentinels") in SDKs and middleware that normalizes and validates request-scoped telemetry context across transports (HTTP, gRPC, WebSocket, internal queue). The goal is to reduce lost spans during protocol transitions, simplify dual-path propagation compatibility, and provide safe, observable fallbacks when context headers are malformed or trimmed by proxies.
background: We continue to see production cases where traces drop or fragment at ingress/egress boundaries: proxies strip long baggage, mobile clients encode headers differently, and websocket/gRPC bridged flows lose the original trace id. Existing work (see ENG-4927 and ENG-10523) improved instrumentation, but we lack a lightweight, consistent runtime piece in our SDKs that can assert invariants, perform safe header normalization, and emit metrics when context repairs occur. The sentinel abstraction is intended to be conservative (non-breaking) and opt-in initially.
design_notes:
Key ideas:
- Sentinel = small object instantiated per request that encapsulates: trace_id, span_id, parent_id, sampling_decision, and a sanitization/logging policy.
- Pluggable hooks: transport adapters provide a minimal read/restore API (extract, inject, repair).
- Repair strategies: map legacy header names -> canonical, truncate oversized baggage sets preserving high-value keys, and fall back to server-generated context with a 'repaired' tag.
- Observability: emit a structured metric 'telemetry.sentinels.repaired' with labels {transport, reason} and a low-cardinality tag for service.
- Backwards compatibility: sentinel injection never overwrites an existing valid trace id unless an explicit policy is enabled by the host app.
- SDK surface: Node/Python/Go shims exposing middleware for Express/FastAPI/net/http and interceptors for gRPC.
- Performance: microbenchmarks target <50ns/op overhead on hot path for minimal sentinel checks; heavy repairs are async where safe.
- Security: sentinels do not persist or log PII; repair actions are deterministic and reversible when possible.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (SDK surface + local tests):
- Add sentinel type to node/python/go SDKs with extract/inject/repair APIs.
- Implement HTTP middleware for Express and net/http, plus gRPC interceptors.
- Unit tests: header permutations, oversized baggage, legacy header names.
Phase 2 (integration + metrics):
- Wire metrics emission to telemetry pipeline and add dashboard tiles.
- Add end-to-end tests across proxy chain (nginx->edge->service) in staging.
Phase 3 (rollout):
- Canary deploy in staging to 10% of traffic, monitor repaired-tag traces and error rates.
- Gradual production rollout with opt-in config; default disabled for Private deployments until audit.
Deliverables:
- SDK changes (three repos) + integration PRs.
- Confluence design doc and an observability dashboard for sentinel metrics.
- Migration guide for customers wanting stricter repair policies.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for all extract/inject/repair code paths across SDKs.
- Staging scenario tests simulating header truncation, proxy header renaming, and websocket upgrade with context.
- Load test to measure latency overhead at QPS representative of production (10k rps per node).
- Test matrix: Node 18, Python 3.11, Go 1.21, nginx 1.22 proxies.
- Run synthetic traces through tracing pipeline to ensure 'repaired' tag surfaces in trace search and trace sampling policies are unaffected.
rollout_plan:
- Feature gate: runtime config 'telemetry.sentinels.enabled' default false for Private tenants; true for Redwood-hosted beta customers.
- Canary: enable for internal services (mesh-internal) first, then PLG accounts that opt-in.
- Monitor: telemetry.sentinels.repaired (rate), traces with repaired=true (sampled), and any increase in 5xx or latency P50/P95 on edged services.
- Rollback plan: flip feature gate off; any in-flight repair is non-destructive.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose sentinel APIs and middleware/interceptors for HTTP and gRPC
End-to-end staging tests pass with <1% span loss in proxy-truncated scenarios
Metrics for repaired events are emitted and visible in the new dashboard
Performance overhead remains under 0.3% p99 latency in baseline load test
Confluence doc with migration and ops guidance published and reviewed by SRE/SEC
